instruction:
The marked line (>>) of a TypeScript/Svelte file uses an identifier containing the word "node". Which ONE of these meanings does the word carry at that site?
- graph-vertex ("entity"): A subject in the user's knowledge base: the thing statements are made about. What a person means when they point at a circle in the graph view. Scope: THE ONLY ONE OF THE FOUR NODES THAT IS OURS TO NAME, and the codebase already has a better word for it: entity, used 927 times across 183 files. Prefer entity in data and logic; reserve node strictly for the RENDERED representation of an entity (see kterm:rendered-node).
- node-runtime ("Node.js"): The JavaScript runtime the build, the MCP server and the offline scripts run on. Scope: Only ever appears as a proper noun or in a node: import specifier. It is never a domain term, and it must never be shortened to node in prose where a reader could take it for an entity.
- rdf-node ("RDF term"): One of the three kinds of thing that can occupy a position in an RDF triple. Defined by RDF and the RDF-JS interface, not by this project. Scope: Appears in src/lib/rdf/types.ts as NamedNode and BlankNode. These names are fixed by the specification — do not rename them, and do not reuse the word for our own vertex concept.
- rendered-node ("entity marker"): The drawn representation of an entity in the 2D or 3D view — its position, colour, icon, label and hit target. A presentation object, not data. Scope: This is where most of the 947 bare uses of node actually live (src/lib/3d/, nodeMap, nodeColors, nodePositionCache). Renaming these is FREE and is the highest-value cleanup available, because it is exactly the collision with three.js.
- scene-object ("scene object"): A member of a three.js scene graph — a mesh, light, camera or group. Three.js's own hierarchy concept. Scope: Threlte is the precedent worth copying: it does not rename the foreign thing, it namespaces it, so THREE.Mesh becomes <T.Mesh> and the origin stays visible. Qualify our own uses rather than competing for the word.
- other: none of the above (a DOM node, a generic tree node, Node.js, or an unrelated word).
Judge from what the code does with the value, and the file path. Give the meaning id and a reason under 20 words.
